text:
I added a fourth Redis node and our cache hit rate fell off a cliff.

No errors. Just... every key seemed to miss. The database got hammered overnight.

The bug was `hash(key) % N`. When N changes, almost every key maps to a new server. Resharding looked like a cache wipe.

Consistent hashing fixes that: keys live on a ring, each server owns an arc. Add one node → only keys on that arc move (~1/N of the total). The rest stay put.

Virtual nodes spread load more evenly when you have few physical servers.

Same idea shows up in CDNs, shard routing, and load balancers — anywhere you resize a pool without wanting a thundering herd on the backend.

Full write-up with ring diagrams and the mistakes I made the first time.

https://blog.sandeepallala.com/blog/system-design-consistent-hashing
